title: The Forthcoming Migration Storm
author: Robert Hunziker
content:
[![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/sebastien-
goldberg-AW5MxlFDVzc-
unsplash-680x453.jpg)](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/08/07/the-
forthcoming-migration-storm/)

![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/sebastien-
goldberg-AW5MxlFDVzc-unsplash-680x453.jpg)

Image by Sébastien Goldberg.

Climate change is the force behind the greatest migration storm of all time.
It will be 500,000,000 or maybe 2,000,000,000 nobody knows for sure how many
but as climate change worsens, the estimates go up. Scientific studies run the
gamut of up to a couple billion homeless wandering the planet, forlornly
looking for a home over upcoming decades.

This is the subject of Josh Fox’s newest film _The Welcome Table_ , 2h 11min,
HBO Documentary Films, June 2026. Fox is best known for his Oscar-nominated,
Emmy-winning 2010 documentary _Gasland._

[Decider](https://decider.com/2026/06/25/the-welcome-table-hbo-max-review-
stream-it-or-skip-it/), the pop culture web site for New York Post reviews
“Stream it or Skip it” rates _The Welcome Table_ “Stream it” … “A Striking and
Memorable Documentary About People Displaced by Climate Change.”

The film is direct and to the point: “One out of every three people is
forecast to leave home due to climate change. The greatest mass migration in
human history is upon us. Governments know this is coming. They’re building
walls and detention centers. Walls stand for racism, nationalism, fascism,
dividing society into unequal separate sides. Walls build misunderstanding.”

Climate change impacts us all because in a very real sense, we’ve all left
home, migrated without really knowing it. We’ve seemingly moved to a climate-
changed planet. This is now home, a different planet, very different from any
we’ve lived on. This is the general view of Josh Fox’s intriguing documentary.

Migrant thoughts: “What tells us we’re welcome? What is home?” serve as
opening statements for what’s lost too easily, forgotten so soon. “Everything
is changing. The steadiness that this world civilization is based upon is
about to evaporate. The climate is changing beyond anything imaginable.”

Early in the film, a long shot of a lengthy wooden table in a green field at
Bywater Levee, New Orleans is the testimonial spot for people to tell true-
life stories. People (strangers) from every continent displaced by climate
change meet for the first time to tell their stories at this long wooden table
on a grassy knoll, wondering: “Where is home now?”

Husband-and-wife fire survivors from Paradise, California (2018). The massive
fire consumed the equivalent of 800 football fields per minute, not per hour,
but per minute! Eighty-five people caught in the inferno, died, real-life
testament to an unforgiving climate that’s drier and hotter than ever before
in human history. This is the current epitome of global warming’s
destructiveness. Nothing is normal now.

Throughout the world, ‘common wildfires’ have evolved into ‘climate infernos’
that are foreign to human experience, as 22,000 displaced Paradise residents
became modern-day refugees, overnight. Fires & storms everywhere and Rain
Bombs coming out of the sky in Brazil kill 50 people, displace unknown
numbers, landslides of mud erupt, forcing homeless migrants to foreign shores
as hometowns are buried.

The unforgiving climate, in part, occurs because the planet’s atmosphere is
much wetter than before. Warm air holds more water vapor, until suddenly
excessive and erupting, cascading all at once, landslides of mud, uprooting
trees, displacing boulders, burying entire towns. Ordinary families, regular
citizens forced to leave, to migrate.

Throughout South America and Central America climate change has destabilized
every aspect of life. It’s either too hot with burned-out agriculture or too
wet with torrential flash floods. People migrate internally within their own
countries or north to the U.S., towards The Wall, but: “Demagogues have always
divided us into who was welcomed and into who was not. And to do that, they
divide us into who is human and who is not.” Trump rally recording: “Animals.
These are animals. They are coming into our country. They are not people… take
a look at the death and destruction that’s been caused by people coming into
this country, caused by people that shouldn’t be here.”

In 2019 the Trump administration announced a new policy for migrants who were
legally seeking asylum. Families with young children would be separated,
thrown into detention camps. The policy was a clear violation of international
law and considered to be child abuse.

**Universal Declaration of Human Rights**

Society challenged blatant human disrespect in 1948 the Universal Declaration
of Human Rights was adopted by the UN, and a brand-new kind of human being was
born. A human being with rights, rights to go anywhere in the world, rights to
leave a country. Violating these rights is a crime against humanity. This
declaration was the legacy of WWII when fascism branded non-whites enemies of
the state, never again.

In 1951 a new definition and protocol was adopted to protect migrants, aka:
Status of Refugees. A refugee was defined as any person who fears being
persecuted for reasons of race, religion, nationality, social status or
politics. And refugees can apply for asylum anywhere in the world simply by
crossing a border. But climate change is not included in these rights. The
definition of refugee does not include climate change as a cause for flight.
Climate change did not exist in 1951. As such, our legal framework is breaking
down in the face of a climate that’s breaking down. In other words: “If the
climate throws you across the border, if it destroys your home, despite y0ur
right to move, you have no legal status and you cannot declare asylum.”

**Calabrian Coast, Italy (2023)**

Josh Fox’s family roots extend to the Calabrian Coast, Italy that became
largely deserted in the early 1900s, a collapsed economy, as Italians migrated
to NYC to find livelihood. Arriving at NYC, they were intimidated by a huge
backlash against Italian migrants. Cartoons in NY magazines depicted Italians
as rats with knives in their teeth, spreading socialism, communism, anarchy at
our doorstep. Cartoons in NY magazines even portrayed “a wall” to restrict
immigration. It’s the same racism, different century, different race. Some
things never change; name-calling is easy to do but eventually sinks into
lowly filthy gutters with a stench that sticks.

**Mediterranean Sea Wall**

The EU essentially uses the Mediterranean Sea as a wall. The Italian military
supplies Libya with warships to patrol migrant rafts, known as the Libyan
Coast Guard. They shoot at rafts full of migrants from Africa, or they return
them to Libya where people are enslaved, raped or extorted for money, tortured
and thrown into arbitrary detention. The world’s media does not see this.

In opposition to the Libyan Coast Guard, SOS Mediterranean is an NGO that
plucks migrants out of the sea. Nevertheless, according to unofficial records
up to 40,000 migrants have likely drowned at sea.

Chris Obuheyi left his home in Nigeria to seek safer shores, ending up in a
small boat across the Mediterranean. He was one of the lucky ones, almost
every person in the rubber raft drowned; he tells a horrifying story of
capture, near death, but he ended up in Sicily and has since become a famous
musician. Nigeria is a country that was, and is, overcome with climate-induced
massive flooding and/or scorching heat that is worse than the iron grip of
Boko Haram, an Islamist terrorist group that terrorizes the countryside. Chris
escaped prison following detention by the Libyan Coast Guard.

**There is a Better Way**

In southern Italy there are many empty towns, empty houses, empty buildings.
Yet, the migrants are shut out of Italy the same way the Italians were shut
out of NYC 100 years ago. But thankfully, there are brave people who embrace
humanity and go against the grain. Mimmo Lucano, mayor of Riace, Italy has a
different view, turning Italian migration policy on its head. “Mimmo Lucano
took the fear of migrants and turned it into love.” Riace opened its doors to
refugees from across the world, creating an immigrant economy that bustles
with success. Mimmo’s name and image “shot into worldwide popularity.”

Mimmo Lucano is “one of the top leaders in the world.” (Forbes Magazine).

Oops, Mimmo was too generous: The government of Italy charged Mimmo with
criminal conspiracy to facilitate illegal immigration and misappropriation of
public property, facing 14 years in jail, realized when the Fox film crew
first arrived in Italy. PM Salvini helped to escalate the hysteria with
Italian mass media, putting out negative stories, blaming immigrants for every
problem in Italy. (footnote: An Italian court has banned Mayor Mimmo Lucano
from office, as of April 29, 2026)

**A Broken Climate System at 1.5C**

Scientists at the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, 10 years ago, saw
“that every fraction of a degree was dangerous… they saw 127 different impacts
(starting at 1:11:35 in the film) of different types of catastrophes” unless
immediate action was taken to cut fossil fuel emissions by 50% within 15
years.

The United States canceled and withdrew from the Paris agreement to cut
emissions on January 7, 2026, via executive order.

Meanwhile, “if we go over 1.5C, all hell breaks loose… even though 200 nations
pledged, the pledges were not observed, and emissions went through the roof.
We never burned this much, this fast. Back in Paris 2015 scientists thought we
would not exceed 1.5C above pre-industrial before 2050, but they were 25 years
off. We breached it in 2025.” Oops!

**Original Home of Humanity Dry as a Bone**

Puriti Gaku from Kenya, the original home of all humanity, was at the table.
But now its rivers have run dry. Turkana of East Africa is the original human
civilization; 150,000 years ago, they spread out all over the globe. They
lived as pastoralist for thousands of years. Puriti Gaku works at Impact
Kenya. The film crew visited Arot’s village, empty straw houses; they’ve all
gone away. All their animals died, taken by severe drought. The one water well
nearly empty, intermittent water barely trickles. Twenty million people in
this region of Kenya suffer from food insecurity. These are the people who did
not cause climate change but feel its worst impact.

Migrants understand the problem: “There is a very clear group of people and
institutions and powers in this world that are trying to convince humanity
that we can save the planet without changing the power imbalances of the
world.”

It won’t happen.

Meanwhile, reality finds a world immersed in risks coming full force so much
faster than ever thought possible.

A charade that pretends to fix climate change is highlighted every year, as
all the nations of the world, except for a handful, meet for two weeks at UN
Conference of the Parties (COP) with 20,000 to 50,000 attendees, well-attended
by oil and gas interests and climate scientists and government bureaucrats,
ongoing for the past 30 years. The principal topic of discussion is climate
change.

After 30 years of intense meetings to fix climate change, it is worse than
ever. Global fossil fuel emissions, like CO2, the primary cause of global
warming, have never been so high. And climate change, like a wild stallion,
has never been so threatening. Alas, every continent, except Antarctica, is
burning.

From afar, distant screams of “stop fossil fuels now” by hundreds of polar
scientists fade away into
[neverland](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/03/27/global-warming-surges-
antarctic-seas-bubble/).

COP 31 is scheduled for November 9-20 at the Expo Center in Antalya, Turkey,
expecting 20,000-40,000 official delegates and other observers, and oh yes,
several prime ministers, presidents, heads of state, and senior politicos
attend for photo ops.
